## What is the current behavior?

report NG8031 as a warning while migrating, set `extendedDiagnostics.checks.ignoredBinding` to

Issues.Title: fix(core): resolve closure and reference retention leaks
Issues.Body:
Resolves several V8 closure-context and reference retention issues across `@angular/core` (similar to #71871):

1. **`injectAsync` (`packages/core/src/di/inject_async.ts`)**: Extracts `createLoader` out of `injectAsync` so the `load` callback attached to `options.prefetch()` does not share a V8 closure context with `injector` (`NodeInjector` -> `LView`).
2. **`ɵɵboundaryUpdate` (`packages/core/src/render3/instructions/boundary.ts`)**: Extracts `createBoundaryResetFn` out of `ɵɵboundaryUpdate` so `$reset` and `details.boundary.reset` do not share a lexical closure context with `nextContainer` or `embeddedLView`.
3. **Incremental hydration triggers (`packages/core/src/defer/triggering.ts`)**: Destructures `blockName` in `setIdleTriggers`, `setViewportTriggers`, and `setTimerTriggers` so scheduled `onInvoke` closures do not retain the `elementTrigger` wrapper object (`{el: HTMLElement, ...}`).
4. **Early event replay listeners (`packages/core/primitives/event-dispatch/src/bootstrap_app_scoped.ts`)**: Calls `removeAllEventListeners` inside `clearAppScopedEarlyEventContract` before clearing `dataContainer._ejsas[appId]` so early DOM listeners on `document.body` (and their closure-captured `q: EventInfo[]` queue) are removed after replay.
5. **Post-hydration listener stashing (`packages/core/src/hydration/event_replay.ts`)**: Only stashes listeners for elements that have a `jsaction` attribute, preventing client-rendered post-hydration elements and their `wrappedListener` -> `LView` closures from accumulating in `JSACTION_BLOCK_ELEMENT_MAP`.
6. **Leave animations (`packages/core/src/render3/instructions/animation.ts`, `node_animations.ts`)**: Moves `allLeavingAnimations.add(lView[ID])` in `ɵɵanimateLeaveListener` from creation time to leave execution time (`runLeaveAnimationFunction`), and ensures `detachedLeaveAnimationFns` is always cleared in `executeLeaveAnimations`.
7. **Signals (`packages/core/primitives/signals/src/computed.ts`, `linked_signal.ts`)**: Clears `node.error = null` when a `computed` or `linkedSignal` recovers from an error state.
8. **HTML sanitization (`packages/core/src/sanitization/inert_body.ts`)**: Avoids storing the first call's `defaultDoc` on the singleton `InertDocumentHelper` instance.

Issues.Title: feat(compiler-cli): add ignoredBinding check
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [ ] Bugfix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [x] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

`<ng-container>`, `<ng-template>`, and `<ng-content>` don't render an element, so Angular ignores
class, style, attribute, and event bindings on them, and every binding on `<ng-content>`. These
templates compile and run without a word:

```html
<ng-container class="card" [class.active]="isActive" (click)="select()">...</ng-container>
<ng-content selector="h1" />
```

Issue Number: #71881

See also: #69322, which this PR also covers: unclaimed property bindings on an explicit
`<ng-template>` get NG8031.

## What is the new behavior?

This is step 1 and changes no behavior that works today. Two breaking PRs build on it, one per
diagnostic, so each can land on its own: #71883 makes NG8032 an error, and #71884 makes NG8031 an
error.

- **NG8031 `ignoredBinding`**, a type-check diagnostic. It needs `strictTemplates`, is
  a warning by default, and is configured through `extendedDiagnostics.checks`, like NG8011:

  ```text
  warning NG8031: The '[class.active]' binding has no effect on <ng-container>, because
  <ng-container> doesn't render an element. Move the binding to an element.

  This check can be disabled using the
  `extendedDiagnostics.checks.ignoredBinding = "suppress"` compiler option.
  ```

  It doesn't report bindings that a directive claims, bindings whose name a matched directive's
  selector uses (they make the directive match), directive host bindings, global event targets, or
  static attributes that a directive, a structural directive, a content projection
  slot, or Angular itself (`ngProjectAs`, `select`, `ngNonBindable`, `ngPreserveWhitespaces`,
  `ngSkipHydration`) reads.

- **NG8032**, a template type-check warning for a component whose selector matches
  `<ng-container>` or `<ng-template>`:

  ```text
  warning NG8032: Component 'Card' matches <ng-container>, but <ng-container> can't host a component
  because it doesn't render an element. Use an element that matches the component's selector
  instead.
  ```

  Today this compiles and fails only when the template renders: dev mode throws an assertion
  ("tags cannot be used as component hosts"), and production mode throws a DOM
  `HierarchyRequestError` when the component's view is attached to a comment node (measured in
  domino, Chromium, and Firefox). It's a warning here because a template that never renders the
  element, such as one behind an `@if` that is always false, runs today. #71883 makes it an error.
  Selectorless `<MyComp:ng-container>` is already a parse error.

- **NG0319**, a dev-mode `console.error` for class, style, and event bindings on
  `<ng-container>` and `<ng-template>`, so JIT is covered too. It's tree-shaken in production.
- **`<svg>` fix:** `[attr.x]` on an `<ng-container>` inside `<svg>` now gets its parse error
  (NG5002), like everywhere else. It failed at runtime before, so nothing that worked breaks.
- The language service no longer suggests DOM attributes on `<ng-container>`.
- Error guides for NG8031, NG8032, and NG0319.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

- The codes are negative (`-8031`, `-8032`, `-319`) because they have guides.
- NG8031 runs as a type-check-block op, `TcbIgnoredBindingsOp`, next to NG8011's
  `TcbControlFlowContentProjectionOp`, and is wired through the same config path. The preprocessor
  backend reports it too.
- The message builder lives in `@angular/compiler` and both backends' recorders use it.
- Known gaps, all on the under-reporting side:
  - Legacy `[@trigger]` bindings and `(@trigger.done)` callbacks aren't reported at compile time.
    At runtime, `(@trigger.done)` on these elements logs NG0319.
  - A root of a multi-root `@if` or `@for` block inside a component's content counts as
    projected when its attributes match a slot, although Angular projects the whole block into
    the default slot. NG8011 already reports that mistake, so NG8031 doesn't add a second
    report for the same attribute.
  - An unclaimed event on `<ng-container>` gets both NG8030 (when `strictUnclaimedEventNames` is
    on) and NG8031. #71884 removes the double report.
- NG8031 found `<ng-content selector="h1">` (meant: `select`) in `packages/examples/upgrade`,
  where it's been since 2017. This PR fixes it, because the repo's build fails on warnings. All
  172 `ng_project` targets in the repo build with this change.

Issues.Title: Report bindings that have no effect on ng-container, ng-template, and ng-content
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/\* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

compiler, compiler-cli, core

### Description

`<ng-container>`, `<ng-template>`, and `<ng-content>` don't render an element. Angular accepts
bindings and attributes on them that can never take effect, and most of them compile and run
without a word:

```html
<ng-container class="card" [class.active]="isActive" (click)="select()">...</ng-container>
<ng-template [title]="label" (click)="missing()">...</ng-template>
<ng-content selector="h1" />
```

Nothing on these lines does anything:

- Class, style, and event bindings on `<ng-container>` and `<ng-template>` are ignored, unless a
  directive claims them.
- Bindings that no directive claims on `<ng-template>` aren't type-checked, so
  `(click)="missing()"` compiles.
- `<ng-content>` ignores every binding, and every attribute except `select` and `ngProjectAs`. The
  `selector` typo (for `select`) silently makes the slot a default slot. Angular's own upgrade
  examples have had this typo since 2017.
- `NO_ERRORS_SCHEMA` hides unknown properties on `<ng-container>`, although no schema can give it
  a property.
- Inside `<svg>`, `[attr.x]` on `<ng-container>` skips its parse error and throws a misleading
  assertion in dev mode.

### Proposed solution

Report what Angular ignores, and nothing that takes effect. Code generation and runtime behavior
don't change.

**Step 1, not breaking:**

- **NG8031 `ignoredBinding`**, a new type-check diagnostic. It needs
  `strictTemplates`, is a warning by default, and is configured through
  `extendedDiagnostics.checks`, like NG8011. It reports class, style, `attr.`, animation, and
  event bindings that no directive claims, every binding on `<ng-content>`, and static attributes
  that nothing reads.
- **NG8032**, a template type-check warning for a component whose selector matches
  `<ng-container>` or `<ng-template>`. That compiles today and fails only when the template
  renders, in dev and production mode.
- The language service stops suggesting DOM attributes on `<ng-container>`.
- **NG0319**, a dev-mode runtime log for class, style, and event bindings on `<ng-container>` and
  `<ng-template>`, so JIT is covered too.
- The `<svg>` parse fix.

**Step 2, breaking:** severities only, in two independent PRs.

- NG8032 is an error.
- NG8031 is an error by default, and NG0319 throws under `errorOnUnknownProperties`.

Every new error points at a binding or component that never worked. NG8031 can be set back to
`"warning"` or `"suppress"`.

Not reported: bindings a directive claims, directive host bindings (directives are reusable),
global event targets, and static attributes that a directive, a structural directive, a content
projection slot, or Angular itself reads.

Question for the team: are the step 2 PRs fine for a minor release, or should they wait for a
major? They can land separately.

PRs: #71882 (step 1); #71883 (NG8032 error) and #71884 (NG8031 error), each building on #71882

### Alternatives considered

- **A template parse error.** The linker re-parses published libraries, so a parse error would
  break libraries that compile today.
- **Only an extended diagnostic.** It can warn, but step 2 needs the same check in the type
  checker. One check in the type checker serves both levels.
- **Only a runtime error.** It reports late, in dev mode only, and can't see bindings on
  `<ng-content>` or which static attributes something reads.
- **Also reporting directive host bindings.** A directive can apply to elements where those
  bindings work, so reporting them would be noise.

Issues.Title: Feature request: Type-safe component CSS with implicit "$styles" in templates
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

compiler, compiler-cli

### Description

Angular provides style encapsulation but doesn't type-check CSS class references in templates. Renaming or removing a class from a component stylesheet can silently break its usage.

Validating existing `class` attributes or `[class.name]` bindings isn't viable because classes may come from global stylesheets, Tailwind, or third-party libraries.




### Proposed solution


Introduce an implicit, compiler-provided `$styles` object in Angular templates, exposing class names declared in the component's own stylesheets (`styleUrl`, `styleUrls`, or inline `styles`).

**Example:**

```css
/* button.component.css */
.primary { background: blue; }
.loading { opacity: 0.5; }
```

```html
<!-- Existing syntax remains unrestricted -->
<button class="flex items-center" [class.loading]="loading()">
  Save
</button>

<!-- Explicitly type-checked local CSS references -->
<button [class]="$styles.primary">Save</button>
<button [class]="$styles.missing">Save</button>
<!-- Error: 'missing' does not exist -->
```

This could enable compile-time diagnostics, autocomplete, go-to-definition, and rename refactoring across templates and stylesheets.

### Alternatives considered

TypeScript 7.1 content mappers could potentially provide stylesheet-derived types to Angular's existing template type-checking infrastructure.

`$styles` would be a compile-time abstraction resolving to ordinary class names, requiring no runtime object, CSS Modules imports, or changes to Angular's existing view encapsulation.

Angular would control the content mapper and language service highlighting.
Can leverage css modules under the hood. The limitation is not having access to the $styles  object in the ts but existing `@let` synax should be good enough for dynamic class composition directly in the template.

Edge case: `<component [prop]="$styles" (emit)="handler($styles)/>` - can leak into the ts. Which basicaly forces a css module implementation if to be supported. Alternative is compile error.

css modules had been rejected before when used "as is", but this is a controlled angular api that would leverage content mappers so it deserves a discussion.

Issues.Title: compiler: `void` inside a constant array or object literal throws in `PureFunctionConstant.keyOf`

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

In `@angular/compiler` 22.2.5, compiling a template with an array or object literal whose entries are all constants and include a `void` expression throws an unhandled error in both AOT and JIT compilation.

```js
import '@angular/compiler';
import { ɵcompileComponent } from '@angular/core';

class App {}
ɵcompileComponent(App, { template: '{{ [void 0, 1][1] }}' }); // or '{{ { a: void 0 }.a }}'
console.log(App.ɵcmp);
```

It should compile without error and pool the constant literal, just as it does for `{{ [typeof 0, 1][1] }}` or `{{ [!true, 1][1] }}`. The `void` operator is supported in template expressions, but `GenericKeyFn.keyOf` is missing a case for `VoidExpr` alongside `TypeofExpr`.

Issues.Title: Hydration writes values that the server already rendered, which restarts playing videos
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

core

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

During hydration, Angular writes values that the server already rendered, and the browser reacts to each write.

A video with `autoplay` starts playing as soon as the browser parses the server HTML. When Angular hydrates the page, the video jumps back to the start. All of these templates have the problem:

```html
<video src="clip.webm" autoplay muted></video>
<video [src]="clip" autoplay muted></video>
<video [attr.src]="clip" autoplay muted></video>
```

There are two causes:

- `elementLikeStartShared()` calls `setupStaticAttributes()` on every element, including DOM nodes reused from the server. It writes each static attribute, the static `class`, and the static `style` again.
- On the first update after hydration, attribute and property bindings write their values, because they have no previous value to compare with.

In Chrome, writing the same value to `src` restarts the load algorithm of a media element. Writing the same `src` to an `<iframe>` loads a new document. I checked the `<iframe>` case in plain JavaScript, not in an Angular app.

The writes also cost time. On a table with 300 rows of static classes, ARIA attributes, and SVG icons, hydration makes 12,961 attribute writes, and 12,871 of them keep the same value. After hydration, Chrome restyles 1,247 elements.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://github.com/jsaguet/ngimg-hydration-repro

To see the video restart, run `npm ci`, `npm run build:variants`, and `npm run serve:stock`, and open `http://localhost:4000/media?bootAfterLoad&bootDelay=3000`. The README has screenshots and measurements.

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

No exception. The video restarts during hydration.

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```
Angular CLI       : 22.2.6
Angular           : 22.2.5
Node.js           : 26.11.1
Package Manager   : npm 11.20.0
Chrome            : 156
```

### Anything else?

A draft pull request follows with one possible fix. It writes a value during hydration only if the DOM has a different value. The problem stands if you prefer another approach.

A fix affects event handlers that run today only because of these writes. For example, a `(canplay)` handler on a video that was ready before hydration runs once today, because the video restarts. It wouldn't run after a fix, because event replay doesn't cover `canplay`.

Issues.Title: perf(common): avoid re-setting unchanged attributes in NgOptimizedImage
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [ ] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [x] Other... Please describe: performance

## What is the current behavior?

Part of #71873

During hydration, `NgOptimizedImage` writes all of its host attributes again, with the values that the server rendered. The browser selects the image source again after a write to `src`, `srcset`, or `sizes`, even when the value doesn't change.

## What is the new behavior?

```diff
 private setHostAttribute(name: string, value: string): void {
-  this.renderer.setAttribute(this.imgElement, name, value);
+  if (this.placeholder || this.imgElement.getAttribute(name) !== value) {
+    this.renderer.setAttribute(this.imgElement, name, value);
+  }
 }
```

An image that still has a placeholder keeps today's writes. An image that failed before hydration then fires `error` again, which removes the placeholder. An image that already loaded clears its placeholder before the writes, so it skips them.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

The public API doesn't change. The visible differences are repeated events that were a side effect of the rewrite, described under Risks.

## Other information

### Evidence

On a page with 200 images, hydration takes 28.1 ms instead of 34.8 ms. With 4× CPU throttling, it takes 198.6 ms instead of 247.9 ms. With bound `[width]`, `[height]`, and `[sizes]`, it takes 9.6 ms instead of 23.4 ms. [`results/timings.txt`](https://github.com/jsaguet/ngimg-hydration-repro/blob/main/results/timings.txt) in the [reproduction](https://github.com/jsaguet/ngimg-hydration-repro) has the measurements. The benchmark pages have no placeholders, so the `this.placeholder` condition doesn't affect them.

The extra reads cost 0.05–0.13 ms per 200 images, so they aren't limited to hydration. That comes from a local Chrome microbenchmark of 8 reads on each new image, which isn't part of the reproduction.

Specs in `full_app_hydration_spec.ts`:

- Attributes rendered on the server aren't written again. This spec fails without the check.
- An image with a placeholder is written again. This spec fails without the `this.placeholder` condition.
- A value that differs from the server is still written.

A spec in `event_replay_spec.ts` checks that a `load` event that fired before hydration is replayed, under domino, which doesn't load images. It passes with and without this change.

No spec covers the placeholder image that already loaded, because setting `complete` and `naturalWidth` under domino also runs the dev-mode distortion check, which needs layout.

Test targets for common and platform-server pass, including the Chromium and Firefox suites for common. I couldn't run `image-directive:webdriver_tests` in my environment. That target fails the same way without this change.

### Risks

It affects apps that use `NgOptimizedImage`.

When nothing else writes the attributes of an image that loaded before hydration, `load` no longer fires a second time. That's the case for an image with no static `sizes` attribute (measured in Chrome). A `(load)` handler on that image then runs once, through event replay, which is on by default. Without event replay, it doesn't run. Listeners added imperatively, such as `fromEvent` or `renderer.listen`, aren't covered by event replay and no longer receive that second event.

An image without a placeholder that failed before hydration no longer fires `error` a second time, and the browser doesn't try to load it again during hydration. `(error)` handlers use the same event replay path as `(load)`, but no spec covers it.

This change doesn't address the `sizes` value that changes twice on lazy images. #71873 describes that case.

Issues.Title: NgOptimizedImage makes the browser select each image source again during hydration
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

common

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

During hydration, `NgOptimizedImage` makes the browser select the source of each image again. There are two separate causes.

**The directive writes its attributes again.** `setHostAttributes()` calls `renderer.setAttribute()` for `src`, `srcset`, `sizes`, and six other attributes. The server rendered the same values. A draft pull request skips the writes when the element already has the value.

**The value of `sizes` changes twice on a lazy image.** The directive prepends `auto` to `sizes` on lazy images, so the value that it computes differs from the template. This happens only on a lazy image with a static `sizes` attribute:

```text
server HTML            sizes="auto, 50vw"
hydration, core        sizes="50vw"          setupStaticAttributes() writes the template value
hydration, directive   sizes="auto, 50vw"    setHostAttributes() prepends auto again
```

The directive computes the same value on the server and in the browser, but core's write runs before the directive exists. Each of these two writes really changes the value, so checking for an unchanged value doesn't remove them.

The browser also fires `load` again on images that loaded before hydration. Event replay delivers the original `load` event too, so a `(load)` handler runs twice on those images.

On a page with 200 images, where hydration starts after the window `load` event, hydration takes 35.0 ms today and 27.7 ms with the draft pull request. When the same page uses `[width]`, `[height]`, and `[sizes]` bindings, which core doesn't write to the DOM, hydration takes 9.9 ms with the draft pull request.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://github.com/jsaguet/ngimg-hydration-repro

To see the `(load)` handler run twice, run `npm ci`, `npm run build:variants`, and `npm run serve:stock`, and open `http://localhost:4000/?bootAfterLoad`. A badge under each image counts the calls. The README has the measurements.

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

No exception.

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```
Angular CLI       : 22.2.6
Angular           : 22.2.5
Node.js           : 26.11.1
Package Manager   : npm 11.20.0
Chrome            : 156
```

### Anything else?

Until the `sizes` case is fixed, bind the input, for example `[sizes]="'50vw'"`, so that core doesn't write it to the DOM.

I don't have a proposal for the `sizes` case that I'm confident about. These are the options I looked at:

- Don't prepend `auto` when the template already has it, so that a developer can write `sizes="auto, 50vw"`. This is one condition in the directive. It helps only the templates that change.
- Make the check in core treat `auto, X` in the DOM as equal to `X` in the template. This covers existing templates, but core would then know about something that the directive does.
- Let a directive declare the host attributes that it writes itself, so that core doesn't write them. This covers existing templates, and it adds an internal mechanism for a single attribute.

Which direction would you prefer, if this case is worth fixing?

With canceledNavigationResolution set to 'computed', cancelling the first navigation after a page reload called history.go() with a stale page id and moved the browser to an unrelated history entry. The router started with currentPageId 0 while the restored entry still carried the previous app instance's page id, so the computed delta was non-zero even though there was no previously activated page to go back to.

This differs from #71856: that PR synced currentPageId from the target entry on every NavigationStart while no navigation had succeeded. This PR instead initializes currentPageId once from the restored state at construction, so it tracks the page the router actually starts on, and a later popstate or eager navigation before any success cannot overwrite it. It also resets the browser url to the router's current url when a navigation is cancelled before any navigation has succeeded, so the browser does not stay on a route the router never activated.

Issues.Title: language-server: project reload loop and OOM with a deleted open TS file and solution-style external template (22.2.0)
Issues.Body:
### Is this a bug report or a feature request?

- [x] Bug Report
- [ ] Feature Request

### Summary

Angular Language Service 22.2.0 entered a self-sustaining project-reload/diagnostics loop in a multi-root Nx workspace. A TypeScript file had been deleted on disk while its editor remained open, and an external Angular component template from a different worktree was also open. The server repeatedly failed to find the deleted file's configured project, reloaded/re-analyzed the template's library project roughly every 1–2 seconds, and eventually aborted with a JavaScript heap OOM near 4 GB.

Closing the two editors associated with the deleted path (ordinary editor and Git diff), then running **Angular: Restart Angular Language server**, stopped the loop without reloading VS Code. The external template remained open and its language features worked afterwards.

### Please provide the steps to reproduce the issue [Bug Report only]

**Observed sequence in the affected workspace; not yet independently reproduced in a standalone minimal project:**

1. Open an Nx monorepo in VS Code with multiple linked worktree folders in one multi-root window.
2. Keep an external `.component.html` template open in a library whose `tsconfig.json` is solution-style (`files: []` with references to the library/spec configs). Its sibling component TypeScript editor is not open.
3. Have a TypeScript editor open in another worktree, then delete that TypeScript file on disk while leaving its editor open. In the observed incident, both its ordinary editor and Git diff remained open.
4. The server repeatedly logs `No config file` for the deleted path, interleaved with repeated enabling of the template library project.
5. Within approximately 43–60 seconds per process lifetime, the heap reaches approximately 4 GB and the server aborts. Automatic restarts repeat the same sequence until the language client gives up after five crashes in three minutes.

There is no public minimal reproduction yet; the original workspace is private. The path names and layout below are anonymized. These steps describe the observed state and sequence, not a confirmed universal reproducer.

### Please provide the expected behavior vs the actual behavior you encountered [Bug Report only]

**Expected:** An editor whose file was removed from disk should not cause repeated teardown/recreation and full Angular analysis of another open template's configured project. The server should settle and continue providing template features.

**Actual:** The same project-loading messages repeat about once per second, including repeated `No config file` errors for the deleted TS path. The server exhausts its heap, restarts, and eventually stops restarting. Template diagnostics/navigation become unavailable.

**Recovery observed:** Close only the saved editors for the deleted path, then restart the Angular language server. With the same workspace folders and external template still open, the log settled after about eight seconds. The replacement process remained alive for more than four minutes at approximately 1.4 GB RSS, with no further missing-file messages or crash. Template-to-component navigation was manually verified. This is current-session recovery, not evidence of permanent prevention.

### Please provide the exception or error you saw [Bug Report only]

Representative excerpt, with paths anonymized:

```text
[Info  - 19:44:51] Disabling language service for /workspace/worktree-a/tsconfig.json because project is not an Angular project ('@angular/core' could not be found).
[Error - 19:44:51] No config file for /workspace/worktree-a/libs/backend/src/deleted-file.ts
[Info  - 19:44:51] Disabling language service for /workspace/worktree-b/tsconfig.json because project is not an Angular project ('@angular/core' could not be found).
[Info  - 19:44:51] Enabling language service for /workspace/worktree-b/libs/frontend/shared/tsconfig.lib.json.
[Info  - 19:44:52] Disabling language service for /workspace/worktree-a/tsconfig.json because project is not an Angular project ('@angular/core' could not be found).
[Error - 19:44:52] No config file for /workspace/worktree-a/libs/backend/src/deleted-file.ts
[Info  - 19:44:53] Disabling language service for /workspace/worktree-b/tsconfig.json because project is not an Angular project ('@angular/core' could not be found).
[Info  - 19:44:53] Enabling language service for /workspace/worktree-b/libs/frontend/shared/tsconfig.lib.json.

[3348:0x12800810000] 43091 ms: Scavenge 4014.9 (4071.5) -> 4002.6 (4083.2) MB, pooled: 0.0 MB, 4.70 / 0.00 ms (average mu = 0.527, current mu = 0.565) allocation failure;
[3348:0x12800810000] 43122 ms: Scavenge 4026.8 (4083.2) -> 4011.4 (4090.7) MB, pooled: 0.0 MB, 4.83 / 0.00 ms (average mu = 0.527, current mu = 0.565) allocation failure;

FATAL ERROR: MarkCompactCollector: young object promotion failed Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
[Error - 19:45:28] Server process exited with signal SIGABRT.
[Error - 19:45:28] The Angular Language Service server crashed 5 times in the last 3 minutes. The server will not be restarted. See the output for more information.
```

### Environment

- VS Code: 1.145.0
- OS: macOS 26.6.2, arm64
- Extension: `angular.ng-template` 22.2.0
- Loaded `@angular/language-service`: 22.2.0
- Loaded `typescript/lib/tsserverlibrary`: 6.0.3
- Angular in the affected worktrees: 22.2.4. Other folders in the multi-root window use 21.2.10 and 22.1.8.
- Multi-root window: 35 linked worktree folders
- Server runtime: VS Code's `Code Helper (Plugin)` process
- `angular.server.useClientSideFileWatcher`: enabled (visible in the server arguments)

The same window/folder set was stable for approximately 20 minutes before the deleted-file error/reload loop began. Workspace size may amplify the cost, but does not by itself explain the transition into the continuous loop.

### Suspected mechanism (code-traced; not an isolated reproduction)

There appears to be an interaction between external-template project recovery and TypeScript project cleanup:

1. Project loading calls `enableLanguageServiceForProject`, which performs Angular analysis and `refreshDiagnostics()`.
2. A projects-updated event schedules diagnostics for open files.
3. For the deleted TypeScript file, `getDefaultProjectForScriptInfo` calls `openClientFile`, cannot find a configured project, and reports `No config file`.
4. TypeScript's open-client-file path also runs orphan project cleanup. A solution-style template's association established by `attachToComponentProject` may not be preserved by that cleanup.
5. Processing the still-open external template then calls `loadProjectForExternalTemplate` / `attachToComponentProject`, loading and analyzing the library project again and scheduling more diagnostics.

This is consistent with the repeated log sequence and the observed recovery, but **the exact heap-retention cause and causality of every internal step have not been independently established**.

The recovery methods are present in [14fbe04612](https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/14fbe04612d29460c5d01d6c65cde579f0a42e95), which fixed #69768. This may be a relevant interaction/regression to investigate, not a claim that the commit alone is proven to cause the OOM.

An earlier log episode also showed repeated external-template project reloads and OOMs without a deleted-file error, so a deleted TS file may be one trigger rather than a necessary condition.

Related reports checked: #65356 and #65484 describe older language-service OOM incidents, but do not identify this particular solution-style template/project-reload sequence.

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): add perf tracing to the preprocessor and ng-a…
Issues.Body:
…nalyze

Adds opt-in performance tracing to the preprocessor CLI and the Rust ng-analyze sidecar, controlled by three new flags:

  --perf-trace <path>     write a Chrome trace event JSON timeline
  --perf-summary <path>   write a per-phase summary JSON
  --perf-trace-detail     add per-query async slices and query keys

The trace can be opened in Perfetto or chrome://tracing. The Node driver records its compile phases, with an async slice per file so overlapping files show up correctly. ng-analyze records one slice per poll of each query on the real worker thread that ran it, with flow arrows from the cache miss that requested a query to where it starts executing. Both processes are merged into one file, with the Rust timestamps aligned to the Node clock.

The summary groups time by phase and by query kind (count, self, busy, queued and wall time, plus cache hits and counters like files parsed and filesystem reads), and is meant to be easy to feed into benchmark dashboards.

Tracing is off unless one of the flags is passed. The Rust tracing layer is only installed once an initialize asks for tracing, and each initialize turns recording on or off, so a long-lived sidecar can trace some runs and not others. The Node side uses a no-op tracer otherwise. With tracing off there was no measurable difference in compile time or memory on a compiler benchmark and on two real applications, and outputs were identical. With tracing on, wall time went up about 0.5-1.5% and peak memory about 3-6 MiB, with trace files around 1-2 MB for medium-sized targets.

This adds the tracing and tracing-subscriber crates to ng-analyze. tracing-subscriber is only used for non-wasm targets.

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): drop filesystem type parameter from preprocessor query engine
Issues.Body:
After routing module resolution, component resource resolution, and file
loading through `AnalysisHost`, the `Fs` type parameter on `QueryEngine`
and `QueryContext` no longer described any state the engine holds. It
survived only as a `PhantomData` marker, yet it still forced roughly a
hundred query, evaluator, analyzer, and compiler functions to carry a
`ResourceResolverFs + Clone + 'static` bound and kept the engine's types
tied to the filesystem implementation that hosts are meant to abstract
away.

Make `QueryEngine`, `QueryContext`, and the `QueryCtx` aliases concrete
types and remove the marker field, then drop the bound from every
function, method, and helper type that existed only to thread it
through, including the NgModule scope `ScopeEnv` and `Resolver`, the
streaming coordinator, and `DirtyFilesSnapshot`. The filesystem type now
appears only on the `new`, `new_with_options`, and `new_default`
constructors that wrap a filesystem and resolver in a `DefaultFsHost`, so
existing callers infer it as before, while `new_with_host` and
`new_default_with_host` accept any host directly. Tests that named
`QueryEngine<OverlayFileSystem>` now use the plain engine type, and
imports left unused by the removal are dropped.

Also reword the preprocessor contributor guideline on paths and module
resolution to describe the host boundary: analysis code resolves and
loads only through `AnalysisHost`, only host implementations touch a
filesystem or `oxc_resolver`, path arithmetic applies solely to
path-backed module IDs, and the TypeScript code-generation layer remains
a pure consumer of pre-resolved metadata. There is no change in
behavior.

Issues.Title: fix(core): detect own NgZone by reference instead of instance ID
Issues.Body:
Previously, `NgZone` tracked instances with a module-local `ngZoneInstanceId` counter and
attached `isAngularZone_ID` / `isAngularZone_ID<n>` properties to each forked Angular zone.
`ChangeDetectionSchedulerImpl.shouldScheduleTick()` then checked `Zone.current.get(...)` for
that ID to decide whether a notification happened inside the app's own `NgZone` and could
skip hybrid change detection scheduling.

This breaks down in microfrontend setups where a host application and one or more separately
bundled Angular applications share a page and a global `Zone.js` instance. Because each
bundle has its own copy of `@angular/core`, every bundle starts its `ngZoneInstanceId`
counter at `0` and gets `isAngularZone_ID0`. If one zone-based application invokes a shared
service, callback, Observable, or event that notifies another application while running
inside the caller's `NgZone`, the receiving app's scheduler sees `isAngularZone_ID0` on
`Zone.current`, mistakes the foreign `NgZone` for its own, and skips scheduling change
detection — leaving its views un-updated even when the apps keep their `NgZone`s as siblings.

Instead of assigning per-bundle string IDs, `ChangeDetectionSchedulerImpl` now keeps a direct
reference to `ngZone._inner` and walks `Zone.current`'s `parent` chain checking
`zone === this.innerNgZone`. This preserves behavior for single-bundle multi-app setups and
child zones forked inside an app's `NgZone`, eliminates cross-bundle ID collisions, removes
module-level counter state and the exported `angularZoneInstanceIdProperty` symbol from
`ng_zone.ts`, and avoids string concatenation and property-map lookups on every notification.

Issues.Title: Debug ID changes the bytes of polyfills and main but not their file names, so cached files fail the SRI check
Issues.Body:
### Command

build

### Is this a regression?

Yes. It started with the debug IDs in 22.1.0.

### Description

Follow-up to #34574.

The builder names `polyfills-<hash>.js` and `main-<hash>.js` first. Then it adds a `//# debugId=<id>` line to the file. It computes `<id>` from the source map after it rewrites the map to add `x_google_ignoreList`. The file name does not cover that line.

So when a builder release writes the source map differently, the JS bytes change and the file name stays the same. 22.1.8 did that. Commit 5a0d226b7c moved `x_google_ignoreList` to the start of the map.

With `subresourceIntegrity`, the new `index.html` pins the new bytes. A CDN or browser cache that kept the old file under the same URL serves the old bytes, and the browser blocks the script. This happened to us in production with `polyfills-<hash>.js`.

#34583 fixed this for the chunks of the chunk optimizer. It does not cover files that esbuild names, such as `main` and `polyfills`. 22.2.6 still computes their debug ID from the rewritten map.

### Minimal Reproduction

```bash
npx @angular/cli@22.1.8 new repro --defaults --ssr=false
cd repro
npm install zone.js
npm install -D @angular/build@22.1.6
npx ng config projects.repro.architect.build.options.polyfills '["zone.js"]'
npx ng config projects.repro.architect.build.configurations.production.sourceMap true
npx ng config projects.repro.architect.build.configurations.production.subresourceIntegrity true
npx ng build && mv dist/repro/browser ../build-22.1.6
npm install -D @angular/build@22.1.8
npx ng build && mv dist/repro/browser ../build-22.1.8
```

Both builds write `polyfills-QWJLBG44.js` and `main-HHND32NM.js`. In each file, only the `//# debugId=` line differs:

```
polyfills-QWJLBG44.js
  build-22.1.6: //# debugId=d932f97d-b667-5462-b3b7-b328a1ce7f5a
  build-22.1.8: //# debugId=81c8766a-7d41-50fd-ac6d-16c3c4ed6358
main-HHND32NM.js
  build-22.1.6: //# debugId=e3a30145-1442-57c2-96a7-a88f9bf43b0a
  build-22.1.8: //# debugId=50dd2d3c-f1e3-5224-9587-43f24f562421
```

The two `index.html` files pin different hashes for the same URLs. For both files, the two source maps have the same content in a different key order.

### Exception or Error

```
Failed to find a valid digest in the 'integrity' attribute for resource 'https://example.com/polyfills-JTOAPWZJ.js' with computed SHA-384 integrity '...'. The resource has been blocked.
```

### Your Environment

```
Angular CLI: 22.1.8
@angular/build: 22.1.6, then 22.1.8
@angular/core: 22.2.5
zone.js: 0.16.3
Node: 24.17.0
OS: macOS
```

### Anything else relevant?

Expected: when the bytes of a hashed file change, its name changes too.

A possible fix is to compute the debug ID from the JS before the builder adds the debug ID line, not from the rewritten map. The file name already covers the JS.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): preserve unaffected localized chunk URLs
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows the [guidelines](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines)
- [x] Regression tests were added to the existing i18n suites
- [ ] Docs were updated (no public option changes)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

The application builder adds a digest of the translation files to every JavaScript bundle. Editing one locale can give unrelated chunks new URLs in every locale, forcing browsers to download them again.

Fixes #30675.

## What is the new behavior?

For one-shot browser builds with bundle hashing enabled, compute names after localization. A changed bundle gets a new URL, and bundles that reference it get updated URLs. Unchanged bundles retain their URLs. The dependency graph comes from the esbuild/Rolldown output metadata; JavaScript is parsed when references need to be rewritten or to find worker URLs that are absent from the graph.

Watch, server builds, and builds with custom code plugins keep the existing hashing path.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Measurements and verification

**Chromium 153, warm browser cache.** Changed one French XLF message used by a lazy chunk, switched deployments on the same origin, and opened the page and one independent lazy chunk. JS used immutable cache headers; HTML used `no-store`. All three runs per locale and variant gave the same results. Bytes are Brotli response bodies, excluding headers.

| Locale | JS responses (main → PR) | JS bytes downloaded (main → PR) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| French, translation changed | 5 → 2 | 36,822 → 34,974 (−5.0%) |
| German, translation unchanged | 5 → 0 | 36,596 → 0 |

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): use the workspace package manager in catalog update guidance
Issues.Body:
When `ng update` aborts because a package uses the `catalog:` protocol, the manual migration steps hardcode pnpm and yarn: the install step suggests 'pnpm install' for every package manager except yarn, and the catalog file hint only names pnpm-workspace.yaml and .yarnrc.yml. Bun workspaces also support catalogs, so a bun workspace is told to run 'pnpm install' and to look for files it does not have.

Build the install command from the detected package manager and name the catalog location it actually uses: pnpm-workspace.yaml for pnpm, .yarnrc.yml for yarn, and the 'workspaces.catalog' field in the root package.json for bun. The previous generic text is kept as a fallback when the package manager is unknown.

The new spec fails without the fix: with `packageManager: 'bun'`, the guidance suggested 'pnpm install' and the pnpm/yarn file names.

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): add the missing vi import for toHaveBeenCalledBefore in refactor-jasmine-vitest
Issues.Body:
The `toHaveBeenCalledBefore` transformation rewrites the matcher to a comparison of `vi.mocked(spy).mock.invocationCallOrder` values but never registers `vi` as a pending value import. When the schematic runs with `--add-imports`, the migrated file only imports `expect` and fails to compile with "Cannot find name 'vi'" unless another transformation in the same file happens to use `vi`.

Register the `vi` import when the matcher is transformed, as every other transformation that emits `vi.*` already does.

The new spec fails without the fix: the migrated output contained `import { expect } from 'vitest'` instead of `import { expect, vi } from 'vitest'`.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): preserve component initialization in Karma test bundles
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (not applicable: internal Karma bundling fix; no new options or public API)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

Fixes #34250.

With `@angular/build:karma`, a component imported through a barrel can be captured as `undefined` in another component's `imports` array. This depends on the combination of spec entry points: an async spec importing the component directly can cause lazy module initialization to cross shared-chunk boundaries. The consuming decorator can run before the component is initialized.

The regression fixture includes:

1. A standalone layout component re-exported by a barrel.
2. A dialog importing that barrel and used by two specs.
3. A page importing the barrel and used by another spec.
4. An async spec importing the layout directly.

Against main (`2c6e8b970`), the browser reports **2 failed, 2 successful**. Both dialog specs throw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'ɵcmp')`.

## What is the new behavior?

The Karma build routes the discovered spec entry points through a shared virtual module that imports all selected specs. This keeps spec initialization in one module graph, avoiding the problematic partitioning across independent spec entry points.

- Preserve the existing `spec-*` entry names, including basename-collision handling.
- Keep code splitting enabled so Angular and its testing environment remain shared with the setup entry point.
- Include the original spec files as TypeScript root files, since the build entry points now refer to the virtual module.
- Preserve `include`/`exclude` selection: the virtual module only imports the specs collected by the existing discovery logic.

The same four browser specs now all pass. The added integration test exercises real Karma/Chrome execution rather than only checking generated bundle text.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Simply setting `disableCodeSplitting: true`, as suggested by the earlier Vitest fix in #33729, was insufficient for Karma in this reproduction: it produced testing-environment initialization errors. This change retains shared framework chunks instead.

Validation on macOS arm64, Node.js 24.22.2, pnpm 12.16.1, and Chrome Headless 159:

- `pnpm bazel test //packages/angular/build:karma_integration_tests --config=no-sharding --test_output=errors`: **42 integration specs, 0 failures**.
- ESLint for the changed implementation passes. The repository ESLint configuration excludes builder integration fixtures.
- Prettier checks for both changed files and `git diff --check` pass.

The full repository and E2E suites were not run. Large-suite build size/performance and dynamic addition of spec files during watch mode were not separately benchmarked or validated.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): forward the poll and progress options to the karma build setup
Issues.Body:
The karma builder schema documents the `poll` and `progress` options, but the application build it starts never receives them: `--no-progress` still logs build progress and `poll` does not switch the file watcher to polling. The legacy webpack-based karma builder honored both options.

Forward both values to the build options. No new test since both are pass-through options; the package unit tests cover the compilation of the changed setup.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(@angular/build): forward the poll and progress options to the karma build setup" (#34654)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): report the worktree-local cache in `ng cache info`
Issues.Body:
In a Git worktree the development server keeps its Vite cache in the worktree's own cache directory while the configured path resolves to the shared cache of the main checkout. `ng cache clean` removes both since the `getCacheConfig` localPath addition, but `ng cache info` still reports only the shared path and its size, so the cache that the development server actually writes to in that checkout is invisible.

Print the local path and its size when it differs from the shared path. Outside of a worktree both paths are the same and the output is unchanged.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(@angular/cli): report the worktree-local cache in `ng cache info`" (#34653)

Issues.Title: refactor(@angular/build): remove unused exports
Issues.Body: Remove the `export` keyword from four symbols that are only referenced within their defining file: `calculateThresholds` and `checkThresholds`, whose external callers moved to `checkBudgets` in 4d27c38cd4; `augmentAppWithServiceWorkerCore`, which is only called by the exported wrapper functions; and `getEntryPointName`, whose external call sites were removed in 75abe2cc52. The two threshold functions also leave the unsupported `private` entry point, which re-exports the bundle calculator module; neither `@angular-devkit/build-angular` nor `@angular/cli` references them, and both still compile. The public API golden is unchanged.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "refactor(@angular/build): remove unused exports" (#34651)

Issues.Title: fix(cdk/menu): don't close menu until outside press is released
Issues.Body: Fixes #27878 With a standalone `cdkMenuTriggerFor`, pressing down anywhere outside the open menu closes it immediately, before the button is released. As noted in the issue, the outside click listener never gets a chance: the mousedown blurs the menu, `menuStack.hasFocus` emits `false` and `CdkMenuTrigger` calls `closeAll()`. That means the close can't be cancelled by moving the pointer away before releasing (WCAG 2.5.2 Pointer Cancellation), and it's different from the menu bar and `mat-menu`. I didn't remove the `hasFocus` listener, because it's also what closes the menu when focus leaves it from the keyboard (Tab, or focus moving somewhere else programmatically). Instead, while a root menu is open the trigger now tracks pointer presses on the document: - `pointerdown` outside of the trigger and the menu stack marks that a press is in progress. - If focus leaves the menu during that press, closing is deferred until `pointerup`. - On `pointerup` the menu closes if the pointer was released outside, and stays open if it was moved back onto the menu. - `pointercancel` and closing the menu reset the state, and the listeners are only attached while the menu is open. I listen on the document rather than relying on the overlay's outside click events. A press on the empty area below a short page lands on ``, which the outside click dispatcher (attached to `body`) doesn't see, and the menu would stay open after the release. Focus loss that isn't caused by a press closes the menu right away, the same as before. ### Tests New specs in `menu-trigger.spec.ts` (standalone trigger): - focus leaving the menu without a press still closes it - press outside → focus leaves → menu stays open → `pointerup` outside closes it - press outside → focus leaves → `pointerup` on the menu keeps it open - a press that was already released doesn't stop focus loss from closing the menu ``` bazel test //src/cdk/menu:unit_tests //src/cdk/menu:unit_tests_chromium PASSED //src/cdk/menu:unit_tests_firefox PASSED ``` Without the change in `menu-trigger.ts`, the two press specs fail (`Expected 1 to be 2.`). ### Manual check Standalone trigger + `cdkMenu` with a nested submenu, CDK 22.2.6 and then the same build with this change. I drove it with Playwright using real mouse events, holding the button for 500ms on the page background: | | Chromium 156 | Firefox 157 | WebKit 27.2 | |---|---|---|---| | menu open while the press is held (before → after) | no → yes | no → yes | no → yes | | closed after releasing outside | yes → yes | yes → yes | yes → yes | | press outside, drag back onto the menu, release | closed → stays open | closed → stays open | closed → stays open | | Tab out of the menu | closes → closes | closes → closes | closes → closes | Before, while the mouse button is still held down outside the menu: After:
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(cdk/menu): don't close menu until outside press is released" (#34097)

Issues.Title: fix(cdk/menu): use latest trigger data when menu is reopened
Issues.Body: Fixes #26256 `CdkMenuTriggerBase.getMenuContentPortal()` only creates a new `TemplatePortal` when `menuTemplateRef` changes. The portal captures `menuData` as its context when it's created, so changes to `cdkMenuTriggerData` / `cdkContextMenuTriggerData` were never picked up. The menu kept rendering with the data from the first time it was opened. This also compares `menuData` against the portal's context and recreates the portal when it's a different object. Issues.Title: bug(cdk/scrolling): nested viewports and overlay content inherit the outer `scrollWindow` / `cdkVirtualScrollingElement` scroller
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### Description

`scrollWindow` and `cdkVirtualScrollingElement` provide `VIRTUAL_SCROLLABLE` through `providers`, and `CdkVirtualScrollViewport` takes it with `inject(VIRTUAL_SCROLLABLE, {optional: true})`. So every viewport below them in the injector tree uses the outer scroller, not just the viewport it was meant for:

- a `cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport` nested in the rows of an outer virtual list that uses `scrollWindow` or `cdkVirtualScrollingElement`;
- a `cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport` inside an overlay opened from such a row (`cdkConnectedOverlay`, and therefore also a virtual list inside a `mat-select` panel), even though the overlay isn't inside the scrolling element in the DOM at all.

Such an inner viewport never gets the `cdk-virtual-scrollable` class, so it can't scroll by itself. The mouse wheel scrolls the page or the outer element instead, the rendered range follows the outer scroller, and the rendered items spill out of the viewport box over the following rows.

The docs describe both options per viewport ("add the `scrollWindow` attribute to the `cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport`"), and nothing says nested viewports inherit the scroller. As a workaround, `{provide: VIRTUAL_SCROLLABLE, useValue: null}` on a component between the two viewports makes the inner one scroll by itself again.

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/7ytfjjia-a8v2qj79

It's the docs example "Virtual scrolling window" opened via "Edit in StackBlitz", with only the example file replaced.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Open the StackBlitz. The outer list uses `scrollWindow`, and every row has its own 150px high virtual list with 100 items. The red line under each inner list already says it uses the outer scroller.
2. Hover an inner list and scroll with the mouse wheel: the page scrolls, the list doesn't.
3. The radio buttons at the top switch the outer list to `cdkVirtualScrollingElement` and move the inner list into a `cdkConnectedOverlay`. All four combinations are broken.
4. Select "its own viewport" to compare: the inner lists scroll by themselves.

### Expected Behavior

A viewport nested inside another virtual scroll viewport, or rendered in an overlay, scrolls by itself, the same way it does when the outer list uses its own viewport.

### Actual Behavior

The inner viewport uses the outer scroller (`viewport.scrollable !== viewport`) in all four combinations:

- `scrollWindow`, nested in a row: the wheel scrolls the page, the inner list renders ~40 items that overflow its 150px box and follow the page scroll.
- `scrollWindow`, in an overlay: the wheel scrolls the page instead of the list.
- `cdkVirtualScrollingElement`, nested in a row: the wheel scrolls the outer element.
- `cdkVirtualScrollingElement`, in an overlay: the list can't be scrolled at all and stays on its first 30 items, which overflow the panel.

With an outer list that scrolls itself, both placements work.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.5
- CDK/Material: 22.2.6 (same with 22.3.0-next.5)
- Browser(s): Chrome 157
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): macOS 26

---

Not a regression: the scroller has been injected this way since `VIRTUAL_SCROLLABLE` was added in #24394 (14.1.0). A possible direction: a viewport could act as a boundary for its content, so viewports and overlays declared inside it don't inherit an outer scrollable, and `scrollWindow` could apply only to its own host viewport.

We ran into this with Taiga UI dropdowns that use a virtual scroll inside virtualized lists (taiga-family/taiga-ui#10095).
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "bug(cdk/scrolling): nested viewports and overlay content inherit the outer `scrollWindow` / `cdkVirtualScrollingElement` scroller" (#34095)

Issues.Title: fix(aria/menu): activate interactive content inside menu items
Issues.Body:
### What does this PR do?

Menu items can wrap native interactive elements (a link, a button, an input), but
`Enter`/`Space` only ran the menu's selection logic. The wrapped element was never
activated, so link items and items with `(click)` handlers inside the content were
effectively mouse-only.

`MenuItemPattern` now resolves the interactive element rendered inside the item and
clicks it when the item is triggered. The click bubbles up to the menu's existing
`click` handler, so the item is still selected exactly as it is on a mouse click —
keyboard and mouse now behave the same. Items without interactive content keep their
current behavior, and menu bar items still open their submenu first.

Fixes #34072.

### Testing

- Added unit coverage in `src/aria/menu/menu.spec.ts` for a menu whose items wrap a
  link, a button, and no interactive content at all, asserting that `Enter` and
  `Space` activate the inner element and still report the selection.
- Type checking of the changed sources (`src/aria/private/menu/menu.ts` and
  `src/aria/menu/menu.spec.ts`) passes.
- Note: `bazel test //src/aria/menu:unit_tests` could not be run on my machine because
  Bazel fails to resolve the `rules_sass` toolchain on Windows, unrelated to this change.

Issues.Body: Fixes #34072 The menu's keyboard manager prevents the default action for Enter and Space, and `MenuPattern.trigger()` only called `submit()`. So with the keyboard the item's element was never activated: `` didn't navigate and a `(click)` listener on the item didn't run. Issues.Title: fix(aria/menu): close only the focused submenu on escape
Issues.Body: Fixes #34071 Escape inside a nested `ngMenu` was calling `closeAll()`, so the whole menu tree closed and focus jumped back to the trigger. The APG menu pattern says Escape should close the menu that has focus and put focus back on whatever opened it, and that's also how `cdk/menu` and `mat-menu` already behave. I added a `closeCurrent()` on `MenuPattern` and pointed the Escape binding at it. If the menu is a nested submenu (its parent item isn't in a menubar), it closes just that submenu with `refocus: true`, the same path ArrowLeft/`collapse()` already uses. Otherwise it falls back to `closeAll()`, so first-level menus under a trigger or a menubar close exactly as before. ### Tests New specs: - `private/menu/menu.spec.ts`: Escape from a trigger's submenu, and from a nested submenu under a menubar menu - `menu/menu.spec.ts`: directive test using the existing Berries submenu. Escape from Blueberry leaves the main menu open and focuses Berries ``` bazel test //src/aria/private/menu:unit_tests //src/aria/menu:unit_tests //src/aria/menu:unit_tests_chromium PASSED //src/aria/menu:unit_tests_firefox PASSED //src/aria/private/menu:unit_tests_chromium PASSED //src/aria/private/menu:unit_tests_firefox PASSED ``` I also checked that the new tests fail without the change to `menu.ts` (all three fail with `Expected false to be true.`). ### Manual check I used the repro from the issue (https://github.com/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro, section A): open menu A, go to Categorize, ArrowRight into the submenu, press Escape. The focused element is outlined in red. Before (22.2.6): both menus close and focus goes back to "Open menu A" After (same build with this change applied): the submenu closes, the root menu stays open and focus is on "Categorize" Ref: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/ (Escape: "Close the menu that contains focus and return focus to the element or context, e.g., menu button or parent menuitem, from which the menu was opened.")

Issues.Title: feat(aria/menu): expose the trigger's tabindex as a public signal on MenuTrigger
Issues.Body:
### Feature Description

`MenuTrigger` computes its own tabindex (`0`, or `-1` while its open menu holds the active item) and binds it to the host (`'[attr.tabindex]': '_pattern.tabIndex()'`), but the value is only reachable through the underscored `_pattern`:
https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/aria/menu/menu-trigger.ts#L45

`Menu` already exposes the same thing publicly (`readonly tabIndex = computed(() => this._pattern.tabIndex())`):
https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/aria/menu/menu.ts#L144

The request: add the equivalent `readonly tabIndex` signal to `MenuTrigger`, next to its public `expanded` and `hasPopup`.

### Use Case

A menu trigger inside a roving-tabindex container, such as a keyboard-navigable grid or toolbar not built on `ngToolbar`/`ngGrid`. The container keeps the trigger at `tabindex="-1"` until its cell is active, while the trigger must keep aria's own `-1` while its open menu holds focus. A wrapper directive therefore combines the container's value with the trigger's own, taking the lower of the two.

Today that wrapper has to read `trigger._pattern.tabIndex()`. Deriving it from public state (`expanded() ? -1 : 0`) is wrong while the menu is open but has no active item yet, when aria keeps `0`.

A public `tabIndex` signal would make this composition possible without depending on `_pattern`. An input to let a consumer supply the tabindex would also solve it.

---

pnpm/pnpm (pnpm) ### [`v11.28.11`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.28.11): pnpm 11.28.11 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.28.10...v11.28.11) pnpm 11.28.11 fixes frozen installs with `excludeLinksFromLockfile`, `pnpm link` in workspaces, `pnpm deploy` with dangling symlinks, and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` starting needless installs. ##### Patch Changes ##### Installing packages - `pnpm deploy` now keeps a symlink in the project whose target is missing from the source, such as a link into a `node_modules` directory that was removed after the build. Deploy used to fail with `ENOENT` on such a link [#​17571](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17571). - A package with `bundledDependencies` and a build script now keeps its bundled dependencies when it is restored from the side-effects cache [#​17523](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17523). - `pnpm install` now links the runtime that an earlier `pnpm install --no-runtime` skipped [#​17542](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17542). - Commands of a package whose `bin` paths contain excess parent directory segments, such as `../dist/cli.js`, are no longer missing. Such paths now resolve inside the package [#​17586](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17586). - Generated POSIX shell shims now quote their paths, so shell special characters in a path stay literal. - A repeat `pnpm install` now rewrites the bin shims after `extendNodePath` changes. Before, it reported "Already up to date" and the shims kept the `NODE_PATH` of the previous setting. ##### Lockfile and resolution - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now accepts the lockfile it wrote with `excludeLinksFromLockfile` and `linkWorkspacePackages` on, when a project depends on a workspace package through a plain version range or a `catalog:` entry. It used to fail with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE`. - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm approve-builds`, and `pnpm rebuild` now accept a lockfile that resolves a `*` dependency to a prerelease `latest` version. pnpm wrote such a lockfile and then reported it as outdated [#​17594](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17594). - Packages from the default registry keep plain lockfile keys, even when a prefix such as `npmjs` points at the registry set as `registry`. A dependency written with such a prefix shares the plain entry of the same package. The next install rewrites keys that earlier versions qualified this way [#​17575](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17575). - Relative local paths in root `overrides` now resolve from the workspace root when each project has its own lockfile [#​17691](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17691). Installing a local directory dependency no longer fails when another project's install is writing a lockfile in that directory. - Peer deduplication no longer gives a project different copies of a dependency across direct and transitive paths when an optional peer has no provider [#​17666](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17666). - A Node.js version range such as `>=26.13`, for example in `devEngines.runtime`, now resolves to the newest stable release that satisfies it. pnpm picks a prerelease only when no stable release matches [#​17516](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17516). ##### verifyDepsBeforeRun - With `verifyDepsBeforeRun`, `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` now report dependencies as out of date after a dependency is added to the `package.json` of a local directory dependency, such as `"lib": "file:../lib"`. Before, the command ran without the new dependency installed. - `verifyDepsBeforeRun` no longer reports dependencies as out of sync when only the `version` field of a single-project repository changed [#​17560](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17560). The same holds for a workspace project that no dependency can resolve to. A script run after such a change no longer starts an install first. ##### pnpm link - In a workspace, `pnpm link ` now adds the `link:` dependency to the `package.json` of the project where the command runs, not to the workspace root's `package.json`. The link is created in that project's `node_modules`, as documented. The override is still written to the root `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. - `pnpm link` with several paths now records every linked package in the `overrides` of `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. Issues.Title: fix(material/form-field): support a different direction than the page
Issues.Body:
The form field styles used `[dir='rtl']` selectors, which match any ancestor with `dir="rtl"`. This meant that a form field with `dir="ltr"` inside an RTL page still got the RTL styles: the outline lost its leading border and the label, padding and native select arrow were placed for RTL.

These changes switch the styles to logical properties, so they follow the direction of the form field itself. `transform-origin` and `clip-path` have no logical equivalents, so those two rules use `:dir(rtl)`, which also resolves against the closest element with a `dir` attribute.

Measured in an Angular 22.2 / Material 22.2.6 app (Chromium and Firefox), label offset from the start edge of a `dir="ltr"` field inside a `dir="rtl"` page:

| | Before | After | Plain LTR page |
|---|---|---|---|
| Outline | 29px | 16px | 16px |
| Fill | 65px | 52px | 52px |
| Native select | 33px | 16px | 16px |
| Outline leading border | 0px | 1px | 1px |

Fields in a plain RTL page measure the same before and after.

Fixes #26778.

Issues.Title: fix(material/list): use theme spacing for leading icons in RTL
Issues.Body:
In RTL, the leading icon of a list item had its margins hardcoded to `32px` and `16px`, instead of using the `leading-icon-start-space` and `leading-icon-end-space` tokens like in LTR. The rule has to use physical properties, because icon font stylesheets (e.g. Material Icons/Symbols) set `direction: ltr` on the icon, which makes the logical margins resolve as LTR inside an RTL list. With the M2 values (16px/32px) this happened to look correct, but with M3 (16px/16px, smaller with density) the gap between the icon and the text was twice as large in RTL.

These changes swap the token values in the RTL rule instead of hardcoding them, so RTL mirrors LTR for any theme.

Measured in an Angular 22.2 / Material 22.2.6 app (Chromium and Firefox), edge → icon / icon → text:

| Tokens | LTR | RTL before | RTL after |
|---|---|---|---|
| M3 default (16/16) | 16 / 16 | 16 / **32** | 16 / 16 |
| M3 density -2 (8/8) | 8 / 8 | **16 / 32** | 8 / 8 |
| M2 (16/32) | 16 / 32 | 16 / 32 | 16 / 32 |

Fixes #30537.

Issues.Title: bug(aria/grid): composed cell widgets do not activate when child inputs receive focus
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

A complex GridCellWidget composed through hostDirectives does not enter widget mode when a child input receives focus. The same markup with ngGridCellWidget applied directly works. Focus reaches the input in both cases; the difference is widget activation.

GridCell._getWidget() searches ancestors using [ngGridCellWidget], but this attribute is absent when the directive is composed. As a result, the focusin event is not forwarded to the widget pattern. This concerns widget activation, separately from cell selection in #34074.

Regression status: unknown.

### Reproduction

[Open the minimal StackBlitz reproduction](https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-pbfss5v2?file=src%2Fmain.ts).

1. Wait for the preview to display “Grid widget child focus”.
2. Click the input under “Standard directive”. Its Mode changes from CELL to WIDGET.
3. Click the input under “Composed host directive”. The input receives focus, but its Mode stays CELL.
4. Compare the two implementations in src/main.ts: both use widgetType="complex" and contain an input; the second applies GridCellWidget through hostDirectives.

The displayed Mode reads GridCellWidget.isActivated(). No synthetic events are needed.

### Expected Behavior

Both widgets should enter WIDGET mode when their child input receives focus, so grid navigation is suspended while interacting with the widget.

### Actual Behavior

The standard widget activates. The composed widget remains in CELL mode even though its child input is focused.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.4
- @angular/aria and @angular/cdk: 22.2.6
- Browser: Chrome
- OS: macOS (Apple Silicon)

Also reproduced in the repository Chromium grid tests: the standard control passes and the composed case fails.

Issues.Title: fix(aria/grid): select composed cells when clicking child content
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #34074.

With explicit selection enabled, clicking child content inside a cell composed through `hostDirectives` moves focus but does not select the cell. Clicking the cell host directly works. `Grid._getCell()` searches ancestors using `[ngGridCell]`, but that attribute is absent on composed cells.

Add the static `ngGridCell` host attribute so the existing lookup can find the containing cell. This follows the same approach as #33839 for accordion and adds no signal reads to the grid's host bindings.

Add six regression/control cases covering direct usage, host directives, and inheritance, with clicks on both the host and child content. The tests focus the cell first and verify that the subsequent click changes `aria-selected` from `false` to `true`.

[StackBlitz reproduction](https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-1z1y55cn?file=src%2Fmain.ts) — blue indicates the active cell; a green outline indicates selection. Detailed mouse-click steps are in #34074.

## Validation

- Before the fix: Chromium grid suite reports **75 passed, 2 failed**, for child clicks on composed and inherited cells.
- After the fix: `pnpm test src/aria/grid --no-watch` passes, **77 specs, 0 failures**.
- `pnpm bazelisk test //goldens:aria_api` passes; no API golden changes.

Clicking the padding on the same cell selects it correctly. The reproduction shows a standard grid and a grid using `hostDirectives` side by side. Both use `enableSelection`, `selectionMode="explicit"`, and `multi`. The standard grid selects cells when clicking either their text or their padding. The reusable cell is defined as follows: ```ts @Component({ selector: 'composed-grid-cell', template: '', hostDirectives: [GridCell], }) class ComposedGridCell {} ``` Its content is ordinary markup, for example `Composed: Second`. This makes the clickable behavior depend on whether the user clicks the text or the surrounding padding. ### Reproduction StackBlitz: https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-1z1y55cn?file=src%2Fmain.ts Wait for the preview to load. It uses Angular 22.2.4 and @angular/aria 22.2.6. **Visual indicators:** blue background = active/focused cell; green outline = selected cell. The dashed rectangle marks the child ``; the surrounding padding belongs directly to the cell host. Steps to reproduce with actual mouse clicks: 1. In the first grid, under **Direct ngGridCell**, click the text **Standard: Second** inside the dashed rectangle. The cell turns blue and gets a green outline: it is active and selected. 2. In the second grid, under **hostDirectives**, click the text **Composed: Second** inside the dashed rectangle. The cell turns blue but gets **no green outline**: focus moves, but selection does not change. 3. Click the padding of that same **Composed: Second** cell, outside its dashed rectangle. A green outline now appears: clicking the host directly selects it. Reload the preview to reset the demonstration. ### Expected Behavior With selection enabled, clicking non-interactive child content inside a cell should select the containing cell, just as clicking the cell host does. Using `GridCell` through `hostDirectives` should behave like direct `ngGridCell` usage. ### Actual Behavior | Usage / click target | Focus moves to second cell | Second cell selected | | --- | --- | --- | | Direct `ngGridCell`: child text | Yes | Yes | | `hostDirectives`: child text | Yes | **No** | | `hostDirectives`: cell padding | Yes | Yes | After clicking **Composed: Second** text, its host has `data-active="true"` but `aria-selected="false"`. Issues.Title: bug(aria/menu): Enter on a menu item doesn't activate the element, so link items and (click) handlers are mouse-only
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

Activating a menu item with the keyboard never reaches the item's element:

- `<a ngMenuItem href="...">` (or with `routerLink`) doesn't navigate on Enter.
- A `(click)` handler on `<button ngMenuItem>` doesn't run on Enter.

Clicking either item with the mouse works.

The menu's `KeyboardEventManager` calls `preventDefault()` on handled keys by default (https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/aria/private/behaviors/event-manager/keyboard-event-manager.ts#L34), which cancels the browser's own activation of a link or button. `MenuPattern.submit()` then closes the menu and emits `itemSelected`, but never activates the item itself (https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/aria/private/menu/menu.ts#L404-L421).

Navigation menus are a common use, and the WAI-ARIA APG navigation menubar example is built from `<a role="menuitem" href>` items that Enter follows. With the current behaviour, routing has to be rebuilt by hand in `itemSelected`, which also loses the href behaviours a link gives (open in new tab, etc.).

A possible fix: have `submit()` call `item.element.click()`. That's what native buttons and links do on Enter, and it makes keyboard and pointer activation run the same path.

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/github/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro
Repo: https://github.com/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro (section B; `node check.mjs` runs the steps with Playwright)
Steps to reproduce:
1. Tab to "Open menu B" and press Enter. Focus is on "Go to #target" (`<a ngMenuItem href="#target">`).
2. Press Enter.
3. Reopen the menu, ArrowDown to "Button with (click)" and press Enter.
4. For comparison, click both items with the mouse.

### Expected Behavior

Step 2 navigates to #target, and step 3 runs the item's (click) handler ("(click) ran" appears in the log), the same as clicking them with the mouse.

### Actual Behavior

In both steps the menu closes and focus returns to the trigger, but the URL doesn't change and the (click) handler never runs. Mouse clicks navigate and run the handler.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.4
- CDK/Material: 22.2.6 (@angular/aria 22.2.6)
- Browser(s): Chromium 156
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): macOS

Issues.Title: bug(aria/menu): Escape inside a submenu closes the whole menu instead of only the submenu
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

Pressing Escape while focus is in a submenu closes every open menu and moves focus back to the root `ngMenuTrigger`. `MenuPattern` maps Escape to `closeAll()`:
https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/aria/private/menu/menu.ts#L182

The WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices menu pattern specifies one level: "Escape: Close the menu that contains focus and return focus to the element or context, e.g., menu button or parent menuitem, from which the menu was opened." (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/). The APG navigation menubar example behaves that way.

The other Angular menus already do: `@angular/cdk/menu` closes only the current menu and focuses its parent trigger (https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/cdk/menu/menu.ts#L84-L90), and `mat-menu` does the same. So a menu migrated from CDK or Material to `@angular/aria` changes keyboard behaviour.

If closing the whole tree is intended, an option to close one level would help, similar to Base UI's `closeParentOnEsc`.

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/github/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro
Repo: https://github.com/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro (section A; `node check.mjs` runs the steps with Playwright)
Steps to reproduce:
1. Tab to "Open menu A" and press Enter.
2. ArrowDown to "Categorize" and press ArrowRight. The submenu opens with focus on "Mark as important".
3. Press Escape.

### Expected Behavior

Only the submenu closes. Focus returns to "Categorize", and the root menu stays open.

### Actual Behavior

Both menus close and focus returns to the "Open menu A" trigger.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.4
- CDK/Material: 22.2.6 (@angular/aria 22.2.6)
- Browser(s): Chromium 156
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): macOS
